correctness.rationale: With q=2^p and zero-sum loads z, the complete square decomposition has F(q)=2(q−1)−q/n−q(2q−1)/[2q(m−1)−(m−2)] as the sole nonnegative-type obstruction. All other squares carry positive coefficients; if F>0 the explicit critical load realizes positive form. Multiplying F by n[2q(m−1)−(m−2)] gives the claimed quadratic with one root (1,2). Equality has one-dimensional load space and drops affine Euclidean rank exactly one. The unmodified coefficient F0(q)=2(q−1)−q/m−q/n exceeds F(q) by 2q(q−1)/(mh), giving strict exponent improvement and m−2 asymptotics. Independent exact rational zero-sum forms and polynomial checks verified 42 size pairs over four q-values.
